transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um, so I'm here because I just... I feel like my whole life is just one massive, unorganized pile right now. I'm trying to balance my schoolwork, which is already a lot, you know, with all the reading and the assignments, and then I also have this little accessories shop that I run. I make, like, these beaded phone charms and hair clips and stuff? It started as a hobby but now I get actual orders, which is great, but the problem is, I absolutely cannot get them organized at the same time. 

It's like, if I focus on school, my shop falls apart, and if I focus on the shop, I completely miss my school deadlines. My bedroom and my desk are just... it's a total disaster. I have my jewelry supplies, like all these tiny beads and spools of wire, literally mixed up with my due date planners and loose shipping receipts from the post office. And then my assignment notes are just scattered everywhere in these huge, messy piles. I look at it all and I just freeze. I have absolutely no idea what to do first. I'll pick up a receipt, then see a school note, then drop them both because I remembered I need to mail a hair clip, but then I can't find the padded envelopes. It's just so frustrating because I really want to do well with both things, but the receipts and the notes and the supplies... they just end up everywhere, and I really just don't know how people keep it all straight.
When you feel overwhelmed by all the things you need to do and the mess around you, how does that affect your mood or emotions? Do you find yourself feeling anxious, sad, or hopeless about it?

Um, sad or hopeless? No, I don't think I feel like that. Like, I don't sit on my bed and cry about the receipts or anything. And hopeless sounds so... I don't know, heavy? Like, I know I'll eventually get the orders out, even if it takes me forever. I actually really love making the charms, and I love my customers—they're always so sweet when they message me on Instagram to ask for custom colors. So I'm definitely not sad or depressed about my life. 

And as for being anxious... I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed feeling panicked or anything like that. It's more just this really intense, buzzing frustration. Like last Tuesday, for example, I had this big order for three custom phone charms, and I was standing there looking at the pile of padded shipping envelopes mixed in with my history textbook and all these loose little glass star beads that had spilled out of their container. And I didn't feel sad, I just felt... I don't know, annoyed? But just annoyed at the mess, not like the world was ending. I just kind of stood there and sighed really loudly, and then I think I just walked into the kitchen and made a sandwich because I didn't even know what to do with myself. 

So yeah, I wouldn't say I feel anxious or sad or hopeless at all. I just... I'm not really sure what the exact word for it is, honestly. I just know I don't feel those specific things you mentioned.
Can you tell me if you have trouble starting or finishing tasks even when they aren't competing with other things, like schoolwork or your shop orders?

Um, yeah, actually, I do. It's not just when I'm, like, trying to juggle a million things at once. Even if I just have one specific thing to do, I still somehow mess it up. Like, if a teacher gives me a list of instructions for an assignment, or even if I'm having a meeting with a vendor—because sometimes I have to talk to the people I buy my bulk charms and wire from, just to make sure I'm getting the right gauge and colors and everything—and they give me, like, a few steps to follow, I always, always mess it up. 

I'll hear what they're saying, and I'll be like, "Okay, got it, step one, step two, step three," and I'll jump right in and do the first part. Like, I'll fill out the top half of the worksheet, or I'll confirm the bead colors with the vendor. But then, later on, I'll find out that I completely skipped something super important. Like, I'll hand in the assignment and the teacher will be like, "Where's the attached form?" and I'm just standing there like, "What form?" Because I completely forgot that was part of the instructions. Or with the shop stuff, I'll think I finished an order note for a custom piece, and then I'll realize I never actually finished writing down the last part of what the customer wanted, like if they wanted a silver clasp instead of a gold one. 

It's just... it happens all the time. I start off really strong, doing exactly what I was told, and then somewhere along the line, the rest of the instructions just vanish from my brain. I don't mean to do it, obviously. I really try to listen. But it's like my brain just takes the first step and runs with it, and completely drops the rest of the list. And it's so annoying because then I have to go back and fix it, which takes even more time, and I'm already so behind on everything as it is. So, yeah, even when there's no competing tasks, just following through on a set of instructions is really, really hard for me.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of disorganization, difficulty following through on instructions, and problems completing tasks, even in the absence of competing demands, strongly suggest ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. Symptoms are pervasive across settings (school and work), and there is no evidence of significant mood symptoms to support a depressive or anxiety disorder. No features of psychosis, bipolar disorder, or neurocognitive disorder are present.
